title: Reliability guild sprint protocol and stakeholder matrix
content:
Purpose:
This doc defines an experiment-first sprint protocol for the newly-formed Reliability Guild to coordinate SLO definition, ownership handoffs, and lightweight cross-team playbooks. The goal is to reduce friction in launching service-level objectives and to create a predictable, low-overhead cadence for fast iteration and rollbacks.

Overview (one-liner):
A two-week sprint pattern combining a 5-day discovery window + 5-day delivery window, explicit stakeholder matrix, and three lightweight templates (SLO proposal, rollback trigger, postmortem-lite).

Why this exists (context):
- We have disparate SLO practices across product teams: different metrics, different alert thresholds, inconsistent on-call responsibilities.
- Past launches often defer SLO signoff until late in development, causing rework and missed targets.
- The guild model should create a shared runway: standard templates, a regular forum for tradeoffs, and clear ownership handoffs.

Protocol at a glance:
- Cadence: 2-week sprint aligned to engineering fortnight.
- Sprint split: Week A = Discovery & coordination; Week B = Delivery & verification.
- Weekly touchpoints: Guild sync (Mon 30m), SLO review board (Wed 60m during Week A), Ops dry-run (Thu 45m in Week B).
- Decision window: All SLO proposals must receive tentative signoff by end of Week A to proceed to delivery.

Roles & stakeholder matrix (quick):
- Service Owner (team that owns the service): proposes SLO, responsible for implementation and initial dashboards.
- Reliability Guild Lead (Maya Singh): coordinates reviews, escalates cross-team conflicts, owns guild calendar.
- Platform/Infra Rep (Ethan Park): availability and cost implications, deployment constraints.
- Product/PM Rep (Ruth Chen): user impact tradeoffs and prioritization.
- Oncall & SRE Liaison (Liam O'Connor): alerting, runbook integration, oncall load estimate.
- Security/Compliance (as needed): sign off for data-sensitive metrics or private deployments.

Templates (attached as small sections below):
1) SLO Proposal (one-page):
   - Service name, owner, channel.
   - User journey & critical path.
   - Candidate SLI (metric, collection method, aggregation window).
   - Target & time-window (e.g., 99th percentile latency < 200ms over 30d, or availability 99.95% monthly).
   - Rationale & user impact buckets (none/minor/major).
   - Cost sensitivity note: estimated delta in GPU-hours or request units.
   - Rollout plan: gradual percentages & fallback model variant.
   - Acceptance criteria for delivery.

2) Rollback Trigger (short):
   - Trigger metric(s) and threshold (e.g., error rate > 2% sustained for 5m).
   - Automated vs manual rollback decision owner.
   - Immediate mitigation steps (circuit-breaker, model fallback, route to lower-cost replica).
   - Notification list and Slack channel.

3) Post-delivery check (postmortem-lite):
   - 7-day smoke metrics snapshot versus baseline.
   - Any incidents or near-misses.
   - Small improvements backlog (max 3 action items).

Discovery week activities (Week A):
- Day 1 (Mon): Guild sync: quick pitches (3 min) of SLO proposals. Decide which proposals advance.
- Day 2 (Tue): Deep-dive office hours: infra and SRE reps validate metric instrumentation feasibility.
- Day 3 (Wed): SLO review board: cross-functional scoring (risk, cost, user impact).
- Day 4 (Thu): Acceptance criteria and rollout plan refinement; fill SLO Proposal template.
- Day 5 (Fri): Tentative signoff / move to delivery; coordinate delivery owners.

Delivery week activities (Week B):
- Day 6 (Mon): Kickoff for delivery; infra changes scheduled in CI windows.
- Day 7 (Tue): Instrumentation and dashboards live in staging; smoke tests scheduled.
- Day 8 (Wed): Ops dry-run: simulate alerts and rollback procedure.
- Day 9 (Thu): Canary rollout (10% traffic) + close monitoring.
- Day 10 (Fri): Evaluate against Acceptance criteria; ramp or rollback.

Decision rules & escalation:
- If SLO causes > 20% predicted cost increase, Platform/Finance must approve before ramp.
- If instrumentation is not feasible within Week B, halt and reschedule with clear blockers listed.
- Conflicts between Product and Reliability Guild escalate to Director-level (cc: eng leads) with a one-week forced-decision window.

Measurement & guardrails:
- Baselines: all proposals must include a 30d baseline for the chosen SLI.
- Signal quality: request-level sampling 1% minimum for latency SLIs or full-ed instrumentation for critical metrics.
- Alerts vs SLO reporting: alerts set conservatively; SLO burn charts drive long-term decisions.

Communication norms:
- Use #reliability-guild for asynchronous threads and decisions.
- All signoffs recorded as a single-threaded comment on the SLO proposal Linear ticket.
- Weekly digest: auto-posted summary of wins, blockers, and experiments concluded.

Lightweight experiment examples (to test protocol):
- Experiment A: Introduce a latency SLO for “embedding generation” path; test canary with smaller batch sizes to measure latency vs cost tradeoff.
- Experiment B: Try prefix caching for chat sessions on a single service; measure token cost reduction and SLO impact.

Success criteria for the guild pilot (6 weeks):
- 6 SLO proposals processed through the protocol with documented outcomes.
- >80% of proposals have instrumentation ready within delivery week.
- Reduction in late-stage SLO rework by 50% compared to prior quarter.
- At least one measurable cost-saving experiment completed and documented.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Teams view the guild as extra approval gate. Mitigation: keep templates lightweight, limit review to 60m, emphasize experiment nature.
- Risk: Instrumentation gaps slow progress. Mitigation: a small infra earmark for quick instrumentation patches (1-2 engineer-days per sprint).

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should the guild maintain a small "fast path" for emergency SLOs (security, compliance) that bypass weekly cadence?
- What is the exact cost approval threshold (finance vs platform)? Propose keeping at 20% for pilot.
- Who owns the canonical SLI library and dashboard templates? (Proposal: Platform team with Guild curator rights.)

Next steps (immediate):
- Confirm pilot participants: Service owners for two initial experiments (assign by 2026-02-13).
- Reserve recurring calendar: Guild sync Mon 10:00am PT, SLO review Wed 9:00am PT.
- Create Linear epic and three tickets: template migration, instrumentation fund, and pilot experiments.

Notes to self / quick TODOs:
- Draft the SLO Proposal template in Confluence and link it (Maya).
- Ask finance for temporary approval waiver for experiments under $2k (Ethan).
- Book Ops dry-run sandbox window on staging next Friday (Liam).

Appendix: quick SLO Proposal checklist (copyable):
- [ ] Service name & owner listed
- [ ] User journey defined
- [ ] SLI metric & collection method specified
- [ ] Baseline included (30d)
- [ ] Target & window chosen
- [ ] Rollout plan & rollback trigger defined
- [ ] Cost delta estimated
- [ ] Acceptance criteria stated

End of doc.
